svg.title: What the model reads, as raw text
svg.desc: The raw text that a small model read and wrote during one task in the simple harness: the harness's instructions, AGENTS.md, the skill list, the tool list, the task, one tool call that reads a skill, the result and the answer, each matched to a row of the context window in part 1.
svg.text: What the model reads, as raw text

The simple harness ran one task with Gemma 4 E4B, a small open model that runs on your own computer. Its /raw command printed the model's whole window. Each section of it matches a row of the window in part 1.
What /raw printed
The model reads these tokens from top to bottom.
You are a coding agent. You help with one task at a time in a project folder.
Reply in plain, short sentences, and give only what the task asks for.
# AGENTS.md
This is the web shop of a small bakery. The code is in src/ and the tests are in test/.
- Write in British English.
- Name issues by their number, such as #42.
# Skills
A skill is a file with steps for one kind of task. When a task matches a skill, first read the skill's file with the read tool, then follow its steps.
- commit-message: Write a commit message for a change. File: skills/commit-message/SKILL.md
- release-notes: Write release notes for a new version. File: skills/release-notes/SKILL.md
# Tools
You have one tool, read, which returns the text of a file in the project folder.
To use it, reply with one line like this and nothing else:
CALL read("skills/release-notes/SKILL.md")
The program then replies with RESULT: and the text of the file.<turn|>
Write a commit message for my fix of issue 123: src/session.ts now reads the timeout in milliseconds, so users are no longer logged out after a minute.<turn|>
CALL read("skills/commit-message/SKILL.md")<turn|>
RESULT: ---
name: commit-message
description: Write a commit message for a change.
1. The first line says what the change does, in at most 50 characters. It starts with a verb, such as Fix, Add or Remove.
2. Then comes an empty line.
3. Then one or two sentences say why the change was needed.
4. The last line is "Fixes" and the issue number, when the change fixes an issue.<turn|>
Fix: Adjust session timeout to milliseconds
The session timeout was previously set incorrectly. This change updates it to use milliseconds, preventing premature logouts.
Fixes #123
Rows of the window in part 1
Colours and numbers match part 1.
Harness's own instructions (system prompt)
AGENTS.md: your project's rules, full text
Skill list: a name and a description per skill
Tool list: one tool, read
YOU
Write a commit message for my fix of issue 123
MODEL
TOOL
The commit-message skill: steps to follow
MODEL
The commit message, in the skill's format
SENT FIRST, EVERY TIME
THE CONVERSATION, GROWING DOWNWARDS
Markers such as <|turn>user and <turn|> come from the chat template in the model file.
They mark who wrote each part, and the model learned them in training.
The model only writes text. The harness finds the CALL read(...) line with a regular
expression, reads the file and asks the model for its next reply.
The harness sends the file back in a new turn that starts with RESULT:. From here on, the skill
is in the window for every reply.

Recorded on 15 November 2026 with harness.py, llama-cpp-python 0.3.35 and gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_0.gguf (ggml-org/gemma-4-E4B-it-GGUF on Hugging Face), at temperature 0.2 with seed 0. Models trained for tool calls have their own format for calls and a separate role for results.
